nodes.title: Part 1: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Part 1. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: A Pod contains a main application container and a second container that ships logs to a centralised logging backend. The two containers share the same network namespace and filesystem. Which multi-container Pod design pattern does this represent?
flashcards.back: A Sidecar container runs alongside the main container in the same Pod, sharing its network and storage. It extends or enhances the main container without modifying it — common use cases are log shipping, metrics collection, certificate rotation, and service mesh proxies (e.g., Envoy/Istio). Ambassador proxies outbound traffic. Adapter normalises output format. Init containers are sequential pre-start containers.

flashcards.front: A developer needs to ensure that a database is ready before the main application container starts. The check should run once and exit before the application Pod begins. Which Kubernetes feature is BEST suited for this?
flashcards.back: Init containers run sequentially before any app containers start. They must complete successfully (exit 0) before the next init container or the main containers begin. An init container that checks database connectivity (e.g., using `nslookup` or a TCP check script) is the idiomatic Kubernetes approach for dependency ordering. Liveness/readiness probes run after the container has already started.

flashcards.front: A developer runs `kubectl get pods` and sees a Pod in `Init:0/2` status. What does this mean?
flashcards.back: The `Init:X/Y` status in kubectl output means X of Y init containers have completed successfully. `Init:0/2` means the Pod has 2 init containers defined and the first one is still running (or hasn't started yet). The main application containers will not start until all init containers complete with exit code 0.

flashcards.front: A developer needs to run a batch process that completes a specific number of tasks in parallel. The Job should process 10 items, running 3 tasks at a time. Which Job spec fields control this behaviour?
flashcards.back: `spec.completions` defines the total number of successful Pod completions required (10). `spec.parallelism` sets how many Pods can run concurrently (3). Kubernetes creates new Pods as existing ones finish until `completions` is reached. `activeDeadlineSeconds` limits total Job duration; `backoffLimit` limits retry attempts after failure.

pairs.stem: A developer needs to ensure that a database is ready before the main application container starts. The check should run once and exit before the application Pod begins. Which Kubernetes feature is BEST suited for this?
pairs.option: An init container that runs a connectivity check and exits 0 only when the database is reachable

pairs.stem: A Pod contains a main application container and a second container that ships logs to a centralised logging backend. The two containers share the same network namespace and filesystem. Which multi-container Pod design pattern does this represent?
pairs.option: Sidecar — the second container augments the main container with an additional function (log shipping)

pairs.stem: A developer needs to run a database cleanup script every night at 2:30 AM. Which Kubernetes resource should be used, and what schedule string is correct?
pairs.option: DaemonSet with spec.updateStrategy.rollingUpdate.scheduledTime: '02:30'

pairs.stem: A developer has deployed a new application version and needs to check the rollout history. The current version has a problem and the team wants to revert to the previous revision. Which kubectl commands are used in sequence?
pairs.option: kubectl get deploy -o yaml → kubectl apply -f previous-version.yaml

pairs.stem: A developer wants to run a privileged monitoring agent Pod on every node in the cluster, including nodes added in the future. Which workload resource ensures one Pod per node automatically?
pairs.option: StatefulSet with one replica per node

pairs.stem: A developer runs `kubectl get pods` and sees a Pod in `Init:0/2` status. What does this mean?
pairs.option: The Pod has completed 0 of its 2 init containers and is waiting for the first to finish

nodes.title: Networking fundamentals: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Networking moves packets between machines using layered protocols (the OSI / TCP-IP stack). Most exam questions test routing decisions, subnetting math, the difference between L2 and L3, and how DNS / DHCP make the whole thing usable for humans.

flashcards.front: What's the difference between Layer 2 and Layer 3?
flashcards.back: L2 (data link) uses MAC addresses to deliver frames inside a single broadcast domain (a switch). L3 (network) uses IP addresses to route packets between networks (a router). Switches do L2; routers do L3.

flashcards.front: How does a subnet mask work?
flashcards.back: The mask splits an IP into a network portion (the high bits, set to 1) and a host portion (the low bits, set to 0). `/24` means the first 24 bits are network = up to 256 hosts (254 usable). `/30` is 4 IPs = 2 hosts — typical for a point-to-point link.

Domain Name System translates human-readable names (`example.com`) into IP addresses. A recursive resolver asks the root, the TLD server (`.com`), and finally the authoritative server for the domain. TTL controls how long answers are cached.

flashcards.front: TCP vs UDP — when do you pick each?
flashcards.back: TCP is reliable, ordered, congestion-controlled — use it when every byte matters (HTTP, SSH, SMTP). UDP is lightweight, no handshake, no retransmit — use it for streaming, gaming, DNS queries, anywhere latency beats reliability.

pairs.stem: A developer creates a Service of type NodePort for a web application. Which statement CORRECTLY describes how this Service works?
pairs.option: NodePort exposes the Service on a static port on every cluster node's IP address.

pairs.stem: A developer needs temporary scratch space shared between two containers in the same Pod. The data does NOT need to persist after the Pod is deleted. Which volume type is appropriate?
pairs.option: hostPath — mounts a directory from the node's filesystem

pairs.stem: A developer creates a PersistentVolumeClaim (PVC) and mounts it in a Pod. If the Pod is deleted and a new Pod is created referencing the same PVC, what happens to the data?
pairs.option: The data is deleted when the Pod is deleted, as the volume lifecycle is tied to the Pod

pairs.stem: A developer needs to pass a database password stored in a Kubernetes Secret as an environment variable `DB_PASSWORD` inside a container. Which Pod spec snippet achieves this?
pairs.option: env: [{name: DB_PASSWORD,.

pairs.stem: A developer creates a Kubernetes Secret to store a database password. After creating the Secret, the developer runs `kubectl get secret db-secret -o yaml` and notices the password is displayed in what appears to be garbled text. What is the correct explanation?
pairs.option: The password is Base64-encoded — not encrypted.

pairs.stem: A developer has two applications — `frontend` (on path '/') and `api` (on path '/api') — both needing to be accessible via a single external hostname. Which Kubernetes resource handles HTTP path-based routing to multiple backend Services?
pairs.option: ExternalName Service pointing to both backends

pairs.stem: A developer needs to schedule a Pod only on nodes with an SSD disk. The nodes are labelled `disk=ssd`. Which Pod spec field pins the Pod to matching nodes?
pairs.option: spec.nodeSelector: {disk: ssd}.

pairs.stem: A developer wants to scale a Deployment named 'web' to 5 replicas without editing the manifest file. Which command achieves this imperatively?
pairs.option: kubectl edit deployment web and change replicas manually

pairs.stem: A developer needs to understand the API version and required fields for a `CronJob` resource without consulting external documentation. Which kubectl command provides this information?
pairs.option: kubectl get cronjob -o json | jq '.apiVersion'

pairs.stem: A developer wants to expose an application inside the cluster using a Service. The application should NOT be accessible from outside the cluster. Which Service type provides internal-only access?
pairs.option: ClusterIP — the default type.

pairs.stem: A developer runs `kubectl get events --sort-by='.lastTimestamp'` to debug a failing Pod. This command shows: 'Failed to pull image: ErrImagePull'. What is the MOST likely cause?
pairs.option: The image name or tag is incorrect.

pairs.stem: A developer needs to add an environment variable to a running Deployment without restarting Pods manually. Which command updates the Deployment's environment in place and triggers a rolling update?
pairs.option: kubectl annotate deployment/web env.NEW_VAR=value

nodes.title: Troubleshooting methodology: Key Ideas
nodes.content: A structured troubleshooting process beats random guessing every time. The classic flow: identify the problem precisely, form a theory, test it, fix, verify, document. Most exams test that you know the flow AND can spot the layer at which the symptom originates.

flashcards.back: CompTIA's 6-step: (1) Identify the problem (gather symptoms, questions to user, recent changes). (2) Establish a theory of probable cause. (3) Test the theory. (4) Plan and implement the fix. (5) Verify full system functionality, apply preventive measures. (6) Document everything.

flashcards.front: Top-down vs bottom-up troubleshooting on a network problem.
flashcards.back: Top-down: start at the application layer and work down — does the browser work? DNS? TCP? Routing? Bottom-up: start at the physical layer — is the cable plugged in? Link light? IP? When you suspect physical/cable, bottom-up is faster. When the user has 'a website is broken', top-down is faster.

Almost every production incident traces back to a recent change — a deploy, a config push, a vendor patch, a cert rotation. 'It was working yesterday' tells you to check today's change-log before forming an exotic theory. Recent changes are the highest-priors of the bug space.

Bisect the path between symptom and cause. If 10 hops between client and server, test hop 5. Good → problem is past hop 5. Bad → problem is before. Two more bisections narrow it to one hop. Faster than checking every link sequentially when the chain is long.

pairs.stem: A developer runs `kubectl top pods` but receives the error `error: Metrics API not available`. What is the MOST likely cause?
pairs.option: The Metrics Server is not installed in the cluster.

pairs.stem: A developer creates a Pod with `imagePullPolicy: Never`. The image `my-app:latest` is NOT present on the node. What happens?
pairs.option: The Pod fails with ErrImageNeverPull — the image must already be present on the node

pairs.stem: A Deployment named 'app' is currently paused (via `kubectl rollout pause`). A developer updates the image and environment variables. When will these changes take effect?
pairs.option: After 5 minutes — the default pause timeout expires automatically

pairs.stem: A developer needs to copy a file from a running Pod to their local machine. The Pod is named 'web-pod' and the file is at `/app/config.yaml`. Which kubectl command achieves this?
pairs.option: kubectl download web-pod:/app/config.yaml ./config.yaml

pairs.stem: A developer generates a Pod YAML template using a dry-run command to speed up CKAD exam tasks. Which command produces a Pod manifest for an nginx container without actually creating the Pod?
pairs.option: kubectl run nginx --image=nginx --dry-run=client -o yaml

pairs.stem: A developer creates an Ingress with TLS configured. The Ingress references a Secret named 'tls-cert' for the HTTPS certificate. What type of Secret must 'tls-cert' be, and what keys must it contain?
pairs.option: Type Opaque with any key name containing the PEM-encoded certificate
